keyVerseText: Of the sons of Hashum; Mattenai, Mattathah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
rootMeaning: The root of מַתַּתָּה (Mattattâh) is מַתִּתְיָה (Mattithyâh), which means 'gift of Jehovah.' This etymology reveals that the name carries a theologically rich meaning, emphasizing that the person bearing it is seen as a divine gift or blessing from God. The root sense highlights a personal relationship with Jehovah, underscoring God's providential role in giving and sustaining life beyond the simple English transliteration as a proper name.
usageInScripture: The word מַתַּתָּה (Mattattâh) appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Ezra 10:33, where it is listed among the sons of Hashum. It is consistently translated as 'Mattathah,' a proper name, which indicates that its primary use is as a personal identifier rather than a common noun. This limited occurrence emphasizes the uniqueness of the individual and situates him within the historical context of the post-exilic community dealing with foreign marriages.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מַתַּתָּה as 'gift of Jehovah' enriches our appreciation for the personal identities recorded in Scripture, reminding believers that each person is a divine gift with a purpose in God's redemptive plan. The historical note that Mattattâh was one who put away a foreign wife during Ezra's reforms points to the seriousness with which covenant faithfulness was maintained. This reflects God's call for holiness and separation for His people, ultimately fulfilled in Christ who is the perfect gift of God. Recognizing the divine gifting in names encourages believers to see their own lives as entrusted by God for His glory.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 10:33 lists Mattathah among the sons of Hashum who took part in the covenant renewal by putting away foreign wives. The inclusion of Mattathah's name, meaning 'gift of Jehovah,' in this list highlights the personal responsibility and identity of those committed to God's covenant. It reminds readers that even individuals with divine names must actively live out their faithfulness, underscoring the call to holiness in the community of God's people.
